title: observability: token-level metrics/tracing/logging + dashboards + alert tuning
author: Priya Nair
body:
Motivation: Improve end-to-end observability for token-level cost and latency, KV cache behavior, and request-level tracing to help SREs and platform engineers diagnose regressions in production. This change centralizes token-level metrics, adds distributed tracing hooks for the serving runtime, improves structured logging for cache events, and ships Grafana dashboards + alert tuning for common failure modes.

What this PR does: - Introduces token-level metrics for request/response token counts, token generation latency distribution (p50/p90/p99), and per-model token cost estimates emitted as Prometheus metrics. - Adds KV cache hit/miss/gap metrics and log fields so we can correlate cache behavior with tail latency. - Hooked in OpenTelemetry spans around critical serving stages (preprocess -> route -> scheduler -> inference -> postprocess) and propagate request_id/topology tags. - Adds structured JSON logging for cache events and model fallback events (includes model_version, shard, request_id). - Adds a set of Grafana dashboards (overview + model detail + KV cache heatmap + cost/latency breakdown) and example alert rules for p99 latency, sudden token cost increases, and cache degradation. - Tuned alert thresholds to reduce noisiness (added rate and cardinality filters, 3m window before firing, and runbook links). - Backfilled lightweight unit+integration tests and e2e smoke test on canary.

Files changed (high level): - telemetry/metrics/token_metrics.rs: new metric definitions and helper to estimate token cost per model. - runtime/tracing/otel_instrumentation.rs: span helpers and semantic conventions. - runtime/cache/kv_cache.rs: emit cache metrics and structured logs on misses/fills/evictions. - services/collector/prometheus_registry.rs: register new collectors and labels. - ops/grafana/dashboards/token_level_overview.jsonnet: top-level dashboard. - ops/grafana/dashboards/model_detail_dashboard.jsonnet: drill-down per-model dashboard. - ops/alerts/token_level_rules.yaml: alert rules and runbook links. - examples/observability/token_level_quickstart.md: README + howto for teams. - tests/integration/token_metrics_e2e.rs: smoke tests for metric emission. - docs/telemetry.md: updated docs for instrumentation conventions.

Testing and validation: - Local unit tests added for metric formatting and cost calc (CI). - Integration tests run in CI against a local minimal runtime — verified spans propagate and metrics expose expected labels. - Deployed to canary cluster for 48h; observed stable metrics, p99 latency improved by fixing a tracing bottleneck (reduced overhead by batching span attributes) and no increase in overall cost. - Alert tuning tested by simulating cache degradation; alerts fired with expected suppression behavior.

Rollout plan: - Feature gate behind observability.token_level flag. - Canary rollout to 5% initially, then 25% after 24h, then 100% after 72h if no regression. - Ops will monitor dashboard panels and cost signal for first 7 days.

Migration notes: - No breaking API changes. - Dashboards added to Grafana provisioning; alert rules require ops to review runbook links and adjust thresholds per customer environment.

Related: ENG-1248 (token-level observability epic), SUP-442 (customer report of unexplained tail latency), ENG-1301 (kv cache metrics backlog).

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke test - [x] Grafana dashboards + JSONNET packaged - [x] Alert rules + runbook links - [x] Docs updated

If merged: follow the rollout plan and notify SRE on #ops-observability with dashboard links and playbook.
commits: Add token-level Prometheus metrics and helpers
Instrument KV cache with metrics + structured logging
Add OpenTelemetry span helpers and semantic convention mapping
Add alert rules and runbook links
review_comments: Ethan Kim: Left a few nits around metric label cardinality. Suggest collapsing 'model_variant' and 'model_revision' into single label to avoid metric explosion.
Priya Nair (author): Agreed. Collapsed labels and added model_tag label with controlled cardinality. Updated tests to assert label set.
Marco Silva: Can you add a short explanation in docs about cost estimation assumptions? Also please confirm the estimated overhead of OTel instrumentation in p50/p99.

Priya Nair (author): Added section in docs explaining cost assumptions (token price lookup table, per-model multipliers) and included canary numbers showing <1% p50 overhead and ~2-3% p99 overhead before batching; batching brought p99 overhead to <1%.
Aisha Rahman: Alert tuning looks reasonable. One suggestion: add a suppression rule for bursty synthetic testing from our staging accounts to avoid noisy alerts.
Priya Nair (author): Added suppression by service_account label and updated alert examples.
release_notes: Add token-level observability: new metrics, tracing spans, structured cache logs, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerts. No breaking changes. Improves ability to diagnose tail latency and token-cost regressions.
notes_for_ops: Dashboards provisioned under 'Observability / Token-level'. After merge, run scripts/provision_grafana.sh in production with credentials and review token_level_rules.yaml. Monitor cost panel for first 72h and mute noisy alerts using service_account label if necessary.
post_merge_actions: Create canary rollout in orchestrator, monitor #ops-observability, collect feedback and adjust thresholds. Schedule follow-up to evaluate 7-day cost impact.
